clue.text: Eclipse to give more light, paradoxically

definitions.meaning: to eclipse a rival is to surpass them so they look dim beside you
to beam more brightly than something else; paradoxical because an eclipse normally blocks light

explanation.surface: An eclipse, oddly, is said to give out more light.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Eclipse' as the astronomical event and the clue seems self-contradictory; it is the verb meaning surpass, which really is to shine brighter than the other party.
explanation.definitionFit: Surpassing someone so completely that they look dim is a standard figurative sense of the verb eclipse.

clue.text: Dutch house in Blenheim? No, surprisingly

definitions.text: Dutch house in Blenheim? No, surprisingly

parts.words: Dutch house in Blenheim? No, surprisingly
parts.note: the Dutch royal house shares its name with an English apple variety, the Blenheim one, not a palace

explanation.surface: Is there a Dutch-style house at Blenheim Palace? Surprisingly, no.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dutch royal family is the House of Orange; Blenheim Orange is an old English apple variety, so the house turns up 'in Blenheim' after all, though not in the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands' ruling dynasty is the House of Orange-Nassau, named for a principality in France.

clue.text: Worst timekeeper, maybe, has breaking news

definitions.meaning: the person who arrives last of all, the least punctual
the most recent report or development

explanation.surface: The worst timekeeper of all has some breaking news.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent news is the newest item, and the least punctual person is the last to arrive.

clue.text: Unexpected death viewed with hostility

indicators.note: the letters of death appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A sudden death is looked upon with hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regarded with loathing or intense dislike is detested.

clue.text: Cause dismay giving almost zero bonus

indicators.note: almost the whole word, with its last letter missing

parts.note: none means zero
a plus is a bonus or advantage

explanation.surface: Staff are dismayed to be given practically no bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or perplex someone so they don't know how to react is to throw them into confusion.

clue.text: Address may show where you're from

definitions.meaning: a formal address is a talk given to an audience
the way you talk, your accent, can reveal your home region

explanation.surface: An address on a letter may show where you live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a postal address, which would also show where you're from; both halves are about the way you talk instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address is a talk delivered to listeners, and a person's way of talking often betrays their origins.

clue.text: Rod grabs Sonia roughly for a dance

indicators.note: the rod holds the next piece inside it, as if gripping it

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: roughly means the letters of Sonia are handled carelessly and jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Rod grabs Sonia roughly to dance with her.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod is a man's name in the surface, not the pole; the dancing pair is a misleading picture of a partner dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stately Polish processional dance in triple time.

clue.text: Sudden emasculation — it's partly for your own good!

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, a stretch of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A sudden castration, it is claimed, is partly for your own benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectal injection given to clear the bowels is a remedy often described as unpleasant but beneficial.

clue.text: Lid on chest designed to display tools

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: the letters of chest are designed into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A chest with a lid has been made to display tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' looks like the chest's cover; it is slang for headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Small axes are common hand tools for chopping wood.

clue.text: Put out triangle as warning

indicators.note: to put something out of order is to disturb it, so the letters of triangle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A triangle is set out on the road as a warning to drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving warning of danger is the act of putting people on their guard.

clue.text: Patron contributes to clinic and hospital department

indicators.note: clinic contributes only its opening part, losing its last three letters

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A benefactor donates money to a clinic and a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributes to' looks like a donor's verb; it signals that clinic gives only part of itself, dropping NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a business is a customer, someone who uses its services regularly.

clue.text: Pub's empty — could indicate some kind of poisoning

definitions.text: Pub's empty — could indicate some kind of poisoning

parts.words: Pub's empty — could indicate some kind of poisoning
parts.note: pub emptied of its middle leaves PB, the chemical symbol of the metal behind a well-known poisoning

explanation.surface: An empty pub might suggest the customers have been poisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the inside letter out of 'Pub' and PB remains: the chemical symbol for this heavy metal, whose poisoning is well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Pb, from Latin plumbum, is the symbol of the heavy metal that causes plumbism, a toxic poisoning.

clue.text: Girl donates heart and liver, for example

indicators.note: the girl gives away her middle letters, the heart of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman becomes an organ donor, giving her heart and liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' pretends to be an organ for transplant alongside the liver; it is the middle of the word Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is an example of an organ that secretes substances, which is what this kind of organ is.

clue.text: To commit perjury may get you into a hole

indicators.note: the letters of the following words may be got into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Committing perjury might land you in a hole, in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is the crime of telling a falsehood after swearing to be truthful in court.

clue.text: Having lasted remarkably some flowers form them

indicators.note: something done remarkably is done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some flowers that have lasted remarkably well form a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' are things that flow, rivers, not blooms: rivers form these fan-shaped mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers, the crossword's flowers, deposit silt at their mouths into triangular land formations.

clue.text: Glass box with compass

parts.note: the box and the tele are both British slang for television
compass means range or extent, as does scope

explanation.surface: A glass-topped box containing a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' suggests the navigation instrument; here it means range.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass, or glass for short, is an old name for a hand-held optical instrument for seeing far away.

clue.text: Possibly swallow the wrong way? Allow a little water

indicators.note: the word for the swallow is read in the wrong direction, from end to start

parts.note: a swallow is one example of a bird, hence possibly
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: If you swallow the wrong way, let a little water go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' pretends to be the verb of choking on a drink; it is the bird, whose word turned round gives DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a small quantity of liquid, such as a few drops of water.

clue.text: Lie around, definitely relaxed

indicators.note: the letters of lie are moved around

parts.note: surely means definitely

explanation.surface: Lie around, definitely a relaxed way to spend the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie around' reads as a phrase for lounging, which fits the definition; around is in fact the anagram signal on lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried and easygoing describes something done at a relaxed pace.

clue.text: Dancing m-masters show these impediments

indicators.note: the letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancing masters with a stutter show their speech impediments.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'm-masters' is itself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech hesitations that repeat sounds are a well-known kind of impediment.

clue.text: To agree completely

parts.note: taken as written
two accounts that tally agree with each other

explanation.surface: Asking someone to agree with you in every respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something entirely, with nothing left out, is doing it fully or wholly.

clue.text: Tall story leads to your arrest — reveal nothing!

indicators.note: the leads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A tall story leads to your arrest, so don't let anything slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling or exaggerated tale is informally called this, as in spinning one.

clue.text: Very small turnover, perhaps, could have you in tears

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for very small
a turnover is a kind of pastry, one example of a pie

explanation.surface: A tiny financial turnover might make you cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business revenue, which would fit the tears; it is a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-jerking sentimental film is informally called this because it makes audiences cry.

clue.text: Ladylike, yet mostly masculine

parts.note: the word for ladylike ends in the five letters of a word meaning masculine, so most of it is

explanation.surface: Someone who is ladylike yet largely masculine.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in the spelling: five of the seven letters spell MANLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Having qualities associated with women, such as being ladylike, is the core sense.

clue.text: Old PM's country acres

definitions.meaning: belonging to Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974
open uncultivated land, scrubby moorland in the countryside

explanation.surface: The former Prime Minister's estate in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a Conservative UK Prime Minister in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracts of open, wild land covered with low shrubs are found in rural Britain.

clue.text: Two thousand houses are lost, destroyed in fearsome current

indicators.note: the two letters standing for thousands enclose the rest, as a house holds its occupants

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM

indicators.note: the words are lost and destroyed, their letters wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two thousand homes have been lost, wiped out by a terrifying flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' turns ARE LOST into AELSTRO, and 'houses' puts that between the two Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool of great violence is a powerful swirling body of water that can drag ships down.

clue.text: Reject old footballing legend? Not entirely

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: the legend's name is not given entirely, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: Should we reject the old footballing legend? Not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims the final E from PELE.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out or banish someone, such as a pupil, is to reject them forcefully.

clue.text: Produce audible bird calls

indicators.note: what is heard spoken stands in for the spelling

parts.note: caws are the harsh calls of crows and rooks

explanation.surface: Make some bird calls loud enough to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or give rise to an effect is to make it happen.

clue.text: Capital's a vital element in business

definitions.note: the clue's capital-is, with the 's as a link

indicators.note: the element sits within the abbreviation for business

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
air is one of the four classical elements and vital for life

explanation.surface: Capital is a vital ingredient in running a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' seems to mean money, which fits business; it is a capital city, Egypt's.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Nile is the capital of Egypt.

clue.text: Take on just half of them — a clever move

indicators.note: only the second half of the word them is used

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Hire only half of those applicants: a shrewd tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on staff is to hire them, giving them work.

clue.text: Episode in The Detectives, possibly ten to follow

parts.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of ten could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An episode of a TV detective drama, with ten more to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Detectives' looks like a TV series title; in British crosswords it is the CID, the police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence, especially a notable one.

clue.text: Fighter doesn't need one to join up

indicators.note: the fighter does without the following item, so it is removed

parts.note: a soldier is a fighter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fighter needs nobody's help to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up' pretends to mean enlist, fitting the fighter; it means fusing metal parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Solder is the act of fusing metal parts together with a melted alloy.

clue.text: They convey much the same, in other words

definitions.text: They convey much the same, in other words

parts.words: They convey much the same, in other words
parts.note: words with closely matching meanings say much the same thing using different words

explanation.surface: Things that say much the same thing, put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of near-identical meaning express the same idea in alternative vocabulary.
